title: Three Doors
product: Futures, options, crypto exchanges (as a case study), arbitrage funds
philosophy: Know your intent before you act

lessons.title: Three doors
lessons.subtitle: Why are you making this trade?
lessons.capability: Tell apart hedging, speculation and arbitrage from a trade's intent.

steps.speaker: dash
lines: I bought a coin because it'll moon. My uncle sold wheat futures. My cousin buys on one exchange and sells on another. We're all investors!

steps.speaker: kip
lines: You're all trading, but behind three different doors.
Hedging reduces a risk you already have. Speculation bets on a price move. Arbitrage catches a price gap between two markets.

steps.title: Intent Detective
steps.caption: Swipe each case to its door (← ↑ →), or tap a door.

steps.question: A farmer locks today's wheat price for her harvest. That's…

options.why: Yes. She already has wheat; she's removing the price risk.
She isn't betting on a move. She's avoiding one.
There's no price gap between two markets here.

steps.question: Buying a share because you think it'll double by Friday is…

options.why: Right. A bet on a price move, with no risk being reduced.
Nothing is being protected.
Friday isn't long term!

steps.title: In real life
steps.realLife: The same instrument, like a futures contract, can hedge, speculate or arbitrage. What matters is why you use it. Ask yourself first: which door am I walking through?
steps.deeper: Exchanges and SEBI watch for manipulation in all three. In India, retail speculation in F&O grew so fast that SEBI tightened the rules in 2024, raising contract sizes and limiting weekly expiries.

lessons.title: Speculation and leverage
lessons.subtitle: Borrowed power cuts both ways
lessons.capability: Explain leverage and why it can wipe out an account on a small move.

steps.speaker: dash
lines: My app lets me trade 10× my money! ₹10,000 controls ₹1,00,000. If it rises 10%, I double!

steps.title: The leverage dial
steps.caption: Set the leverage, then try different market moves.

predict.question: With 10× leverage, a 10% fall does what to your ₹10,000?
predict.reveal: 10 × 10% = 100%. The whole ₹10,000 is gone, and the broker closes your position (a margin call).

options.why: Yes. It's a magnifying glass, not a shield.
If only. Losses are magnified exactly the same way.
Gains too. That's the temptation.

steps.question: Why do most F&O speculators lose money?

options.why: Right. Small moves are mostly noise, every trade costs money, and leverage magnifies the mistakes.

options.text: The markets are closed too often
options.why: Not the reason.
Most aren't hedging at all.

steps.title: In real life
steps.realLife: SEBI found that about 9 in 10 individual futures and options traders lost money between FY22 and FY24, with net losses of over ₹1.8 lakh crore. Leverage is a big part of why.
steps.deeper: Margin is the deposit a broker demands for a leveraged position. If losses eat into it, you get a margin call: add money now or be closed out at a loss.

lessons.title: Arbitrage Rush
lessons.subtitle: When is a price gap free money?
lessons.capability: Explain arbitrage, and why fees and delays make most gaps unprofitable.

steps.speaker: dash
lines: Bitcoin is cheaper on Exchange A than on B! I'll buy on A and sell on B. Free money!

steps.speaker: kip
lines: That's arbitrage. But check the fees on both sides, and how long the coins take to move.
Gaps often close before you get there.

steps.title: Arbitrage Rush
steps.caption: Two exchanges tick side by side. Trade only when the gap beats the fees, and it might hold.

steps.question: An arbitrage trade only pays when the gap…

options.text: Beats the fees and survives the delay
options.why: Yes. Fees on both sides plus the risk the gap closes in transit.
A tiny gap loses to fees.
The coin doesn't matter; the maths does.

steps.question: Why do big price gaps rarely last?

options.text: Many traders rush to close them
options.why: Right. Arbitrage is fiercely competitive, so gaps vanish fast.
Prices are set by buyers and sellers.
They don't, which is why gaps appear at all.

steps.title: Card unlocked: Crypto
steps.realLife: In India, crypto gains are taxed at 30% with 1% TDS on transfers, which kills most small arbitrage. A regulated version exists: arbitrage mutual funds earn the small gap between share and futures prices.
steps.deeper: Arbitrage funds buy shares in the cash market and sell the same shares in the futures market, pocketing the gap at expiry. Returns are modest and similar to liquid funds, and they're taxed like equity funds.

lessons.title: Hedging with futures
lessons.subtitle: Asha locks her price
lessons.capability: Explain how a futures contract lets a business remove price risk.

steps.speaker: kip
lines: Meet Asha. She farms wheat. Her costs are fixed, but the price at harvest could be anything.
A buyer offers to fix the price today, with a futures contract.

steps.title: Asha's choice
steps.caption: Fix the price or wait and see? Try a glut, a normal year and a shortage.

steps.question: Asha fixed ₹2,500. At harvest, the price is ₹3,200. She…

options.why: Yes. She gave up the windfall in exchange for certainty.
She agreed to ₹2,500 in advance.
She gets exactly what she agreed.

steps.question: Why would Asha hedge, even knowing she might miss a windfall?

options.why: Right. Hedgers care more about avoiding disaster than about the best possible outcome.
Hedging is the opposite of speculating.
They aren't, and she gives up upside too.

steps.title: In real life
steps.realLife: Airlines hedge fuel prices, exporters hedge the rupee–dollar rate, and farmers' groups can lock crop prices on the NCDEX commodity exchange.
steps.deeper: The person on the other side of Asha's hedge might be a mill that also wants certainty (both hedge), or a speculator who takes on her risk for a possible profit.

lessons.title: Boss: The Detective's Desk
lessons.subtitle: Ten cases, three doors
lessons.capability: Classify trades by intent, and spot speculation dressed up as investing.

steps.speaker: dash
lines: Okay Kip, I get it now. Give me the hardest cases you've got!

steps.title: The big case file
steps.caption: Eight cases. Swipe them all to the right doors.

steps.brief: Three Doors run! Stay calm in the WILD lane, keep a cash cushion, and dodge Dash's hot tips.

steps.question: Someone buys gold to protect savings against rupee weakness. That's closest to…

options.why: Yes. It's reducing a risk they already have.
There's no price gap being caught.
They're not trading in and out.

steps.question: Which door has the most people losing money?

options.why: Right. Especially with leverage and short horizons.
Hedgers usually accept a small cost on purpose.
Arbitrage profits are small, but it's not where most people lose.

steps.title: World complete: Three Doors
steps.realLife: You can now name the intent behind any trade. When an app, friend or influencer pitches a trade, ask: is this reducing a risk, betting on a move, or catching a gap?
